fix: Free the index when the pass ends. Add an ACL2 entry such as fn-rclp-ctx-release that calls (fast-alist-free (fn-rcl-nth 6 ctx)), and call it from an unwind-protect in fnn-owner-reclaim-pass and fnn-log-reclaim-steps. Or build the index with with-fast-alist scoped to the pass.

2026-10-03 Codex source reconciliation: 2f27ae7292dd1069b5d7dd21b8158cd5b3b20f22 is an ancestor of dev 9af0cd1a9. This is a source-landing receipt only; native/proof completion is not inferred, and existing residuals and evidence requirements remain.
reviewer: fn-rclp-index-into (store-reclaim-pack.lisp:84-89) builds a fast alist with hons-acons over every article. fn-rclp-ctx-expiring stores it in the ctx (:631-638). The owner builds a fresh ctx for each dry run or recorded reclaim (owner.lisp:5476, 5674, through fn-owner-orc-ctx at owner-host.lisp:1038-1042). Nothing in the reclaim, expiry or owner paths calls fast-alist-free. The codebase frees fast alists explicitly elsewhere (peer-feed.lisp:275, expiry.lisp:355, served-catalog.lisp:2569), which shows the hash tables are not reclaimed when the alist is simply dropped. Each owner pass therefore leaves an index of every article behind.
scenario: A node with 5M articles runs `store reclaim --recorded`, or the owner's dry-run reclaim, once a day. Each pass allocates a 5M-entry hash table in ACL2's fast-alist table and norms 5M Message-ID strings. ACL2 keeps a fast alist's hash table reachable until fast-alist-free (or until the alist is extended), so dropping the ctx does not release it. Heap use climbs by hundreds of MB per pass until the owner hits its dynamic-space limit.
title: Every reclaim context builds a fast alist of all articles (hons-acons) that is never freed: it leaks in the long-running owner on each reclaim and dry run
